parameters.label: Magnituda sejsmiczna Chicxulub (zakres w literaturze)
parameters.method: scaling: energy-magnitude relations with an assumed seismic efficiency (literature compilation)
parameters.locator: collins2005 Eq. 40 & Table 6 (M=10.4 for 1.65e24 J); richards2015 sect. 'Scaling the Effects of the Chicxulub Impact' (Mw ~9-11 for k=1e-2..1e-5); depalma2019 Abstract & sect. 'Seismic waves' (Mw ~10-11.5); day2005 Abstract (Mw ~11, rendered '<11'); schulte2010 p. 1215 ('magnitude > 11', citing Toon et al. 1997); leveque2024 Sect. 1-2 (Mw 11 adopted)
parameters.notes: No value is measured; all are scaling estimates. Magnitude TYPES differ (Gutenberg-Richter energy magnitude in collins2005 vs moment magnitude Mw elsewhere) and richards2015 note the extrapolation 'depends upon the seismic frequency'. depalma2019 cite meschede2011 for Mw 10-11.5, but meschede2011 state no magnitude. Value 10.5 = middle of the cited span, not a published best estimate.

parameters.label: Magnituda wg wzoru Collinsa (Eq. 40) dla energii referencyjnej 4,184e23 J
parameters.method: scaling: M = 0.67*log10(E) - 5.87 (E = impactor kinetic energy in J, k=1e-4 built in); E_ref = 4.184e23 J (1e8 Mt TNT)
parameters.notes: Range = E from 1e23 to 1.65e24 J (9.54-10.36) widened by +/-0.67 for k = 1e-5..1e-3. Eq. 40 is Gutenberg-Richter log10(Es[J]) = 1.5M + 4.8 with Es = 1e-4 E. Recompute with the energy adopted by the impactor thread: 01-impaktor energy.kinetic_literature = 6e23 J -> M = 10.06; tsunami thread (Range 2022) 2.7e23 J -> M = 9.83.

parameters.label: Sprawność sejsmiczna (ułamek energii kinetycznej -> fale sejsmiczne)
parameters.locator: collins2005 p. 827 'Seismic effects' (1e-4, range 1e-5-1e-3 after Schultz & Gault 1975); meschede2011 source section (k~1e-4 default; 1e-4..1e-5 per Shishkin 2007); khazins2018 Abstract (~1e-3 for impacts, ~1e-5 for airbursts); richards2015 'Scaling...' (1e-2..1e-5); wojcicka2020 Abstract (~1e-6, small Mars impacts)
parameters.notes: Order-of-magnitude uncertainty that maps to +/-0.67 magnitude units. Values for small, low-velocity or porous-target impacts (wojcicka2020) are not directly transferable to Chicxulub. Primary sources Schultz & Gault (1975) and Shishkin (2007) were not opened by me (see openQuestions).

parameters.label: Energia wypromieniowana jako fale sejsmiczne (model referencyjny)
parameters.method: model:meschede2011 (source time function tau vs. efficiency)
parameters.locator: Source model section: tau = 58 s 'corresponds in a crustal environment to an energy of [~1e19] J and k ~1e-4'; tau 20-200 s -> 1e18-1e20 J
parameters.notes: The default energy value is printed as an equation graphic I could not read; ~1e19 J is consistent with k = 1e-4 times the ~1e23 J kinetic energy stated in the paper. Model input momentum dp = 3e19 N s (after Boslough et al. 1996).

parameters.label: Półokres trwania źródła sejsmicznego (funkcja czasowa źródła)
parameters.locator: meschede2011 source section (tau=58 s default; 19 s for k~4e-3; 20-200 s range); leveque2024 Sect. 2 (half-duration 60 s, depth 10 km)
parameters.notes: leveque2024 conclude that matching the Tanis surge would require an effective source process time of 'many minutes' (crater rebound), i.e. longer than this default - see disagreements.

parameters.label: Okres oscylacji krateru (centralne wypiętrzenie) jako źródło fal długookresowych
parameters.method: model: hydrocode crater collapse, as reported by leveque2024 (secondary citation of Collins et al. 2020 and Range et al. 2022)
parameters.notes: Secondary citation - the underlying hydrocode papers were not opened in this thread. Value 300 s = middle of the quoted 200-400 s.

parameters.label: Prędkość grupowa fali Rayleigha (mod podstawowy, 60-310 s)
parameters.method: model:dziewonski1981 (PREM anisotropic; group velocity of fundamental spheroidal modes 0S_l)
parameters.notes: Present-day 1-D reference Earth; values for 0S11 and higher are confirmed correct by the 'Note added in proof'. Lateral heterogeneity changes path averages by a few per cent (3-D model: ekstrom2011). 3.65 km/s is a representative value for 100-250 s; dispersion means long-period (~300 s) energy arrives first, the Airy phase (~230 s, 3.57 km/s) last. Applying to 66 Ma is an extrapolation.

parameters.label: Minimalna prędkość grupowa fali Rayleigha (faza Airy'ego)
parameters.notes: Marks the tail of the R wave train (energy piles up near the group-velocity minimum).

parameters.label: Prędkość grupowa fali Love'a (mod podstawowy, 140-360 s)
parameters.notes: Love waves (G1, G2...) travel ~20% faster than Rayleigh waves and arrive first.

parameters.label: Czas pełnego okrążenia Ziemi przez falę Rayleigha
parameters.method: scaling: 2*pi*6371 km / U_R (U_R = 3.65 km/s; range 3.837-3.568 km/s)

parameters.label: Czas pełnego okrążenia Ziemi przez falę Love'a
Czas dotarcia fali R1 do antypodów Chicxulub
parameters.notes: ~1.52 h. Strong focusing at the antipode (see seismic.antipode_peak_displacement).

parameters.label: Czas dotarcia fali G1 (Love) do antypodów
Liczba okrążeń Ziemi przez fale Rayleigha w ciągu 24 h
parameters.notes: A fixed station sees passages R1, R2, ... up to about R16 within 24 h (two passages per circuit: minor and major arc); detectability limited by attenuation (see amp_factor parameters).

parameters.label: Dobroć Q fali Rayleigha przy okresie ~250 s
parameters.locator: Table V p. 317: 0S32 (250 s) Q obs 180.0, Q com 176.4; 0S35 Q com 168.2
parameters.notes: Used for per-circuit amplitude decay.

parameters.label: Dobroć Q fali Rayleigha przy okresie ~100 s
Spadek amplitudy fali Rayleigha (250 s) na jedno okrążenie (tłumienie)
parameters.method: scaling: exp(-pi*f*t_circuit/Q) with PREM Q and U (0S32-0S35)
parameters.notes: Anelastic attenuation only; geometric spreading on a sphere ~1/sqrt(sin(Delta)) must be applied in addition (antipodal/epicentral focusing). After 24 h the 250-s amplitude is reduced to ~0.1-0.2% by attenuation.

parameters.label: Spadek amplitudy fali Rayleigha (~100 s) na jedno okrążenie
parameters.notes: Shorter periods die out after 1-2 circuits; the late orbits (R5+) are dominated by periods >~200 s.

parameters.label: Spadek amplitudy fali Love'a (~200 s) na jedno okrążenie
Paleo-odległość Chicxulub-Tanis (Dakota Północna)
parameters.method: model: paleogeographic reconstruction (as stated by authors)
parameters.locator: depalma2019 sect. 'Emplacement Mechanism' (~3,050 km); leveque2024 Fig. 2 caption (3,100 km)

parameters.label: Czas nadejścia fali P do Tanis
parameters.method: model: travel times (depalma2019); cross-check ak135/TauP 5.79 min at 27.4 deg
parameters.locator: depalma2019 sect. 'Emplacement Mechanism' (P, S, Rayleigh at 6, 10 and 13 min)
parameters.notes: Cross-check computed in this thread with obspy.taup, model ak135, source depth 1 km.

parameters.label: Czas nadejścia fali S do Tanis
parameters.method: model: travel times (depalma2019); cross-check ak135/TauP 10.47 min

parameters.label: Czas nadejścia fali Rayleigha do Tanis
parameters.method: model: depalma2019 (13 min); scaling 3050 km / 3.837-3.568 km/s
parameters.locator: depalma2019 sect. 'Emplacement Mechanism'; leveque2024 Fig. 2 (largest radial motion ~750-900 s at 3,100 km)

parameters.label: Szczytowe przemieszczenie gruntu (składowa radialna/pionowa) w odl. 3100 km, Mw 11
parameters.method: model:leveque2024 (normal-mode summation, PREMQL6, radial point source Mw 11, half-duration 60 s, 40-500 s band)
parameters.locator: Fig. 2 (value read off the plotted curve, approx. +/-19 m at ~780 and ~890 s)
parameters.notes: Read from a figure, accuracy ~+/-1 m. Long-period band only (no high-frequency shaking). Implies a slow 'heave' of tens of metres over minutes rather than violent shaking at teleseismic distance.

parameters.label: Szczytowa prędkość gruntu w odl. 3100 km (pasmo 40-500 s), Mw 11
Szczytowe przyspieszenie gruntu w odl. 3100 km (pasmo 40-500 s), Mw 11
parameters.notes: ~0.01 g in the long-period band; high-frequency accelerations are not represented by this model.

parameters.label: Szczytowe przemieszczenie gruntu w antypodach
parameters.method: model:meschede2011 (spectral-element; 3-D Earth ~4 m vs spherically symmetric point source 15 m)
parameters.notes: The 3-D heterogeneous, elliptical Earth with a distributed source reduces antipodal focusing by ~4x. Time of maximum not stated in the paper; surface-wave convergence expected at ~1.3-1.5 h (seismic.rayleigh_antipode_time).

parameters.label: Szczytowe naprężenie dynamiczne w antypodach
parameters.locator: Abstract ('in excess of 15 bar'; strain 2e-5; >50 bar in mantle 'chimneys')
parameters.notes: Lower bound ('in excess of').

parameters.label: Szczytowe naprężenia dynamiczne w skorupie/płaszczu górnym (globalnie)
parameters.notes: richards2015 also print '0.1-0.2 strains', evidently a typo (meschede2011 give strains ~2e-5).

parameters.label: Gęstość energii sejsmicznej w górnych ~200 km płaszcza
parameters.notes: Value = geometric middle of the stated order-of-magnitude range. Compared with historical thresholds for triggered eruptions (~0.1-1 J/m3).

parameters.label: Maks. odległość upłynnienia gruntu dla największych trzęsień tektonicznych (analog)
parameters.method: measured (compilation of historical earthquakes, as stated by richards2015)
parameters.locator: 'Scaling the Effects...' paragraph on margin collapse
parameters.notes: Secondary statement; used by richards2015 and day2005 to argue that K-Pg margin failures >1000 km away require an equivalent Mw > 10 source.

parameters.label: Odległość od Chicxulub osuwisk podmorskich na Blake Nose (Atlantyk)
parameters.notes: Lower bound. Mass wasting across ~55 km of the depth transect, water depths 1300-2600 m. Attribution to impact seismicity is the authors' interpretation (tsunami not excluded by the abstract).

parameters.label: Objętość osadów przemieszczonych w Zatoce Meksykańskiej na granicy K-Pg
parameters.method: measured (mapping on borehole and seismic data)
parameters.locator: Abstract (1.05e5 km3 northern Gulf; >1.98e5 km3 gulf-wide)
parameters.notes: Mixed seismic + megatsunami origin according to the authors; deposition 'within days'. Lower bound for gulf-wide value ('over').

parameters.label: Miąższość pokrywy K-Pg (dolny skłon i dno basenu Zatoki)
parameters.locator: Abstract (10-20 m upper slope; 90-200 m lower slope and basin floor)
parameters.notes: Value = middle of the range.

parameters.label: Wysokość fal przyboju (surge) zapisanych w Tanis
parameters.locator: depalma2019 'Emplacement mechanism' ('at least 10 m'); leveque2024 Abstract & PLS (two ~10 m surges)
parameters.notes: Lower bound.

parameters.label: Czas fal przyboju w Tanis po uderzeniu
parameters.method: measured (ejecta spherules embedded in deposit) + model (ballistic trajectories)
parameters.locator: depalma2019 'Chronology of the Deposit' (~13 min to 2 h; spherules from ~15 min; most within 1-2 h); leveque2024 Abstract (within ~1-2 h)
parameters.notes: Timing is bounded by spherule arrival models, which are themselves debated (leveque2024 cite a contrasting view by Artemieva & Morgan 2020).

parameters.label: Amplituda sejsz wywołanych sejsmicznie (wnioskowanie DePalma 2019)
parameters.method: scaling: extrapolation from Tohoku-2011 fjord seiches using magnitude (depalma2019)
parameters.locator: depalma2019 sect. 'Seismic waves' ('of the order 10 to 100 m'); leveque2024 Sect. 1 (resonant seiching 'cannot be scaled up directly from earthquakes to impacts')
parameters.notes: Value = log-middle of 10-100 m. The scaling argument is disputed by later work of the same group; treat as speculative.

parameters.label: Analogia: sejsze w fiordach Norwegii po Tohoku 2011 (8000 km)
parameters.method: measured (eyewitness video, modelled with shallow-water model)
parameters.locator: Abstract (trough-to-peak 1.0-1.5 m; periods 67-100 s; began ~30 min after origin, during S-wave passage)
parameters.notes: Observational analogue for teleseismic seiches (Mw ~9 source; leveque2024 quote Mw 9, depalma2019 Mw ~9.2).

parameters.label: Szczytowe nadciśnienie fali uderzeniowej w powietrzu, 200 km
parameters.method: scaling: Collins 2005 Eq. 54/57 (nuclear surface-burst yield scaling)
parameters.notes: Collins 2005 Eq. 54+57 (1-kt surface-burst fit, px=75 kPa, rx=290 m, r1=r/E_kt^(1/3)) evaluated for E_ref = 4.184e23 J (1e8 Mt). Range: lower = E 1e23 J divided by 5 (authors: for >1e4 Mt the model 'probably overestimates the blast wave effects by a factor of 2-5'), upper = E 1.65e24 J. Uniform-density, flat-Earth assumptions fail at this scale (authors' caveat). Collins 2005 Table 6 values correspond to ~0.5*E in Eq. 54 (not explained in the paper; see thread 07). For the impactor-thread energy 6e23 J: p = 780/175/44/21 kPa and u = 663/261/88/46 m/s at 500/1000/2000/3000 km. At 200 km the site is inside the fireball radius (Collins Table 6: 236 km for 1.65e24 J) and within the ejecta-curtain/plume region, so a separate 'air blast' value has little physical meaning.

disagreements.topic: Seismic magnitude of the Chicxulub impact

positions.claim: M ~10.4 for a 1.65e24 J impact (Gutenberg-Richter energy magnitude with k = 1e-4); ~9.5-10 for 1e23-4e23 J
Mw ~9-11 depending on seismic efficiency 1e-2..1e-5 (E ~3e23 J), frequency-dependent
equivalent Mw ~11 (> 10) required to explain distant slope failure and liquefaction
magnitude > 11 (citing Toon et al. 1997)
Mw 11 adopted as model input

disagreements.assessment: All values are scaling estimates; none is measured. The spread (~9-11.5) is dominated by the unknown seismic efficiency and by mixing magnitude types (energy vs moment magnitude). The geologic argument (margin failure >1600 km away) favours an equivalent Mw >~10, but that inference itself relies on extrapolating tectonic-earthquake liquefaction distances. Use Mw ~10-11 with explicit uncertainty; do not present a single number as fact.

disagreements.topic: Seismic efficiency k of a Chicxulub-scale impact

positions.claim: k ~1e-4 (range 1e-5-1e-3), the 'most commonly accepted figure' from experiments
k ~1e-3 for impacts (explosion-equivalence calculation), ~1e-5 for airbursts
k decreases with impactor size and velocity; 1e-4-1e-5 for Chicxulub (Shishkin 2007, as reported)
k ~1e-6 for small impacts into Martian regolith

disagreements.assessment: No consensus; 1e-4 remains the default in hazard tools but has a 2-order-of-magnitude uncertainty. Small-impact Mars values are not transferable. Keep 1e-4 as reference, propagate 1e-5..1e-3.

disagreements.topic: Origin of the Tanis surge deposit (North Dakota)

positions.claim: Seismically coupled seiche in the Western Interior Seaway triggered by S/surface waves arriving 6-13 min after impact; seiches of 10-100 m plausible

Direct seismic excitation can reproduce ~10 m surges only if the effective source duration is 'many minutes'; resonant seiching cannot be scaled from earthquakes to impacts and needs tens of minutes to develop; alternatives (triggered faulting, slope failure into the WIS, atmospheric waves from the ejecta curtain) remain; mechanism 'incompletely resolved'
A direct tsunami from Chicxulub is excluded by timing (>10 h travel vs 1-2 h window)

disagreements.assessment: The impact-related, sub-2-hour timing is better supported than the specific seiche mechanism. Both main papers share authors; I found no independent peer-reviewed rebuttal (criticism so far mostly in news media, which is not admissible here). Treat the 'seismic seiche' as a hypothesis (contested), the 10-100 m amplitude as speculation.

disagreements.topic: Trigger of Gulf of Mexico / Atlantic margin collapse

positions.claim: Seismic shaking from the impact caused margin collapse and gravity flows (K-Pg 'cocktail')
Sediment redistribution (~2e5 km3) by combined seismic and megatsunami processes, deposited within days

disagreements.assessment: Seismic initiation of slope failure is widely accepted (minutes after S/surface-wave arrival); the relative share of tsunami reworking is not resolved. For the simulation: failures start with shaking, flows and tsunami reworking continue for hours-days.

positions.claim: Peak overpressure from 1-kt nuclear surface-burst data scaled by E^(1/3) (Eq. 54/57); worked example gives 77 bar and 2220 m/s at 200 km for 1.65e24 J
Same authors: the scaling is reliable only for 1-10,000 Mt; above that it probably overestimates blast effects by 2-5x; flat-Earth and uniform-atmosphere assumptions fail

disagreements.assessment: No Chicxulub-specific, peer-reviewed air-blast model was found that I could open. Treat all overpressure/wind values as order-of-magnitude extrapolations; near field (<~300 km) is dominated by the fireball/vapour plume and ejecta curtain rather than by a classical blast wave.

disagreements.topic: Lamb-wave speed and energy scaling (Hunga Tonga analogue)

positions.claim: Lamb-wave group velocity ~315 m/s (theoretical ~310 m/s)
Lamb-wave phase speed 318.2 +/- 6 m/s at surface
Explosion yield 100-200 Mt TNT
Energy release 10-28 EJ; nuclear-test yield relations give unphysically large yields for Hunga

disagreements.assessment: Speed is well constrained (303-324 m/s); energy-to-amplitude scaling is not. Use the speed with confidence; treat any Chicxulub Lamb-wave amplitude as speculation.

disagreements.topic: Speed used for the 'main seismic shaking' arrival

positions.claim: Main shaking arrives at r / (5 km/s) (surface waves in upper crust)
Long-period Rayleigh group velocities 3.57-3.84 km/s and Love 4.38-4.46 km/s (PREM); Rayleigh at Tanis ~13 min (3.9 km/s)

disagreements.assessment: For global propagation use PREM group velocities; the 5 km/s in Collins Eq. 42 is a regional simplification and makes surface waves arrive ~25-30% too early at teleseismic distances.

openQuestions: No peer-reviewed Chicxulub-specific model of the atmospheric Lamb wave or of far-field air blast was found; amplitude, period and nonlinearity of a Chicxulub Lamb wave are unknown (speculative). Interaction with ejecta re-entry heating of the upper atmosphere is unstudied as far as I could find.

South Am. Earth Sci. 176:106058, doi 10.1016/j.jsames.2026.106058 - metadata confirmed via Crossref; abstract not accessible; may contain new seismite/liquefaction evidence and a magnitude estimate.

unverified lead: Morgan, J. V.; Bralower, T. J.; Brugger, J.; Wünnemann, K. (2022) The Chicxulub impact and its environmental consequences, Nat. Rev. Earth Environ., doi 10.1038/s43017-022-00283-y - paywalled; recent review that may update seismic/blast statements.
Exact wording of the magnitude in day2005 (OpenAlex renders 'moment magnitude <11'; leveque2024 cite 'Mw 11'; richards2015 cite 'Mw > 10') needs checking against the GSA original.

unverified lead: Lay et al. (2005) Science 308:1127 and Park et al. (2005) Science 308:1139 (Sumatra 2004) - metadata and abstracts confirmed, but the full texts with multi-orbit surface-wave (R1, R2, ...) observations were not accessible; a peer-reviewed observational statement on how many Rayleigh orbits are visible for Mw 9+ events is still missing here.

unverified lead: Brune, J. N.; Nafe, J. E.; Alsop, L. E. (1961) The polar phase shift of surface waves on a sphere, BSSA 51(2):247-257 (cited by matoza2022) - not opened; basis for the 90-degree phase shift at each antipodal passage (applies to both seismic surface waves and Lamb waves).

Radiation pattern of an oblique (~45-60 deg) Chicxulub impact: froment2024 show impact sources have significant deviatoric (non-isotropic) components, but no published azimuth-dependent amplitude model for Chicxulub was found.

High-frequency (>1 Hz) shaking and Modified Mercalli intensities at Gulf margins and at teleseismic distances are not constrained by any source opened here; collins2005 Eq. 41 uses California attenuation curves (and the unit of Delta in Eq. 41c is not defined in the passage read; continuity with Eq. 41b at 700 km suggests radians).
Western Interior Seaway geometry and depth at K-Pg time are unknown, so seiche periods/amplitudes at Tanis cannot be computed (depalma2019, leveque2024).

Collins 2005 Table 6 airblast values correspond to ~0.5x the impact energy in Eq. 54, which the paper text does not explain; check against the calculator source analysed in thread 07 (Collins et al. 2017 'airblast-energy rule').

Applicability of present-day PREM/ak135 to the Maastrichtian Earth is assumed (differences expected to be small for global travel times); lateral heterogeneity (e.g. ekstrom2011 GDM52) could add a few per cent to surface-wave path times.
